Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

criminal noun and adjective

also criminals, offender, wrongdoer, villain, crook, evildoer, felon

classical

Plaut. Ps. 938
Plaut. Trin. 551 (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Verr. 2.5.144: maleficōrum sceleratōrumque

maleficus, maleficī m.

noun, second declension

an evildoer, a criminal

From male and facere, the one who does wrong. The adjective, criminal, wicked, is maleficus, malefica, maleficum.

Other words

  • sōns, sontis m./f. — the guilty one, an offender

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 3.6; Cic. Phil. 2.18; Traupman 299

    Frequent as a noun, chiefly in the plural, sontēs (Lewis & Short); see guilty.

  • facinorōsus, facinorōsa, facinorōsum — criminal, villainous; as a noun, a criminal

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sest. 81: facinorōsissimī sīcāriī (Lewis & Short); Traupman 151, 299

    Rare but classical; Cicero uses the plural as a noun (Cat. 2.22, Lewis & Short).

  • scelestus, scelesta, scelestum — wicked; as a noun, a villain, a scoundrel

    declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 859; Hor. Epod. 7.1: quō, quō scelestī ruitis?; Traupman 314

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    Common in comedy as a term of abuse, sceleste!; Cicero does not use it of persons (Lewis & Short).

  • crīminōsus, crīminōsa, crīminōsum — criminal

    declension · avoid · modern · Traupman 299

    Traupman’s word for criminals, but classically ‘reproachful, slanderous’ (Cic., Liv.); ‘a guilty man’ only in Cassiodorus (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • neque ego hōc homine quemquam vīdī magis malum et maleficum

    and I have never seen anyone more wicked or more of a villain than this manPlaut. Ps. 938

  • vincula sontium servantō

    they shall keep the prisons for criminalsCic. Leg. 3.6

  • ego hunc scelestum in jūs rapiam exulem

    I’ll drag this villain into court, the outcast!Plaut. Rud. 859

See also crime, thief, guilty, police.
